newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber untraded, seen weak until 1997.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber untraded, seen weak until 1997.

text.p: Rubber futures were untraded by midday on Friday in extremely quiet trade with the market seen drifting until the end of the New Year holidays next week, dealers said.

"I think most of the people are still on holidays. With so many holidays next week here, the market will find it difficult to inspire some play since so many people are not around," a local rubber trader said.
The market will be open until 0400 GMT next Tuesday. It will then be closed on January 1 for New Year and on January 2 for general elections here.
Firmer prices in Japan failed to inspire the market, dealers said. "The mood is very quiet," one dealer said.
At around 0445 GMT, February RSS3 was indicated at 125.00-126.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 126.00 cents.
February RSS1 was indicated at 178.00-180.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.28) a kg from the previous 178.00 cents.
March TSR20 was indicated at 172.00-174.00 Singapore cents (US$1.22-$1.24) a kg from 174.00 cents.
